baselineCritiques.actors: The actors defined are comprehensive and accurately represent the roles involved in the Participium system based on the provided description. All relevant stakeholders (Citizen, Municipal Administrator, Organization Office Staff, Technical Office Staff, External Maintenance Personnel) are included without any omissions or contradictions.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The high-level goals are well-defined, comprehensive, and align with the software description. They cover all functional aspects of Participium, including citizen participation, report processing, collaboration between departments, external company support, notifications, public statistics, and administrative oversight. No contradictions or omissions were found.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are mostly well-aligned with the high-level goals and the software description. However, there is a notable omission regarding the citizen's ability to follow other citizens' reports and receive notifications for them, which was mentioned in section C of the software description. Additionally, the low-level goal "Update report status to 'in progress' or 'resolved'" does not specify all possible state transitions (e.g., moving from "Work in Progress" to "Resolved"), which could lead to incomplete implementation. Lastly, the low-level goals do not address the citizen's ability to send and receive messages through the platform, which is also mentioned in section C.

baseline.description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: https://iris.sad.ve.it/. The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal https://developers.italia.it/.

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section). If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:
- Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved. Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
- Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo). Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description. Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.
highLevelGoals: Allow citizens to report urban issues and track the status of their reports to foster transparency and civic engagement.
Provide a structured workflow for reports to move through approval, assignment, and resolution stages with clear state transitions and accountability.
Enable seamless coordination between technical offices and external maintenance personnel to resolve urban issues efficiently.
Allow external maintenance companies to access and update reports assigned to them, with secure communication channels for internal coordination.
Ensure citizens receive timely updates on report status and communication via platform notifications and emails to build trust in public administration.
Allow non-registered users to view public statistics on report trends and categories to promote awareness and data-driven urban planning.
Provide municipal administrators with private access to detailed statistics and system configuration tools to manage external company access and optimize resource allocation.
lowLevelGoals: Citizen submits a report with location, description, category, and mandatory photo attachment via the web interface.
Citizen views the current state of their report (e.g., pending, assigned, resolved) via the dashboard.
System sends email to citizen when report status updates (e.g., assigned, resolved).
System pushes in-app notification to citizen when report status updates.
Organization Office Staff approves a report to move it to the 'assigned' state.
Organization Office Staff rejects a report with a written explanation and moves it to 'rejected' state.
Technical Office Staff assigns a report to a department or external company based on category.
Technical Office Staff or External Maintenance Personnel updates report status after completing work.
External Maintenance Personnel views reports assigned to them and their current status.
External Maintenance Personnel updates report details and status via a secure login portal.
Citizen views aggregated public statistics on report trends and categories without login.
Municipal Administrator accesses detailed reports, user activity, and system configuration tools.
Municipal Administrator configures which external companies can access and manage reports.
Municipal Administrator generates and exports reports on urban issue trends and resolution times.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are comprehensive and align well with the high-level goals, covering all functional aspects of the system. However, there is a minor omission regarding the "Suspended" state for reports, which is mentioned in the report lifecycle but not explicitly addressed as a low-level goal. Additionally, the interaction between citizens and municipal staff via messages (including chatbots) is partially covered but could be more explicitly defined, especially for external chatbot accessibility.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG omits mandatory registration, email confirmation, and the requirement for up to three photos. It also lacks clarity on the anonymous submission option.

The original HLG is too broad and lacks specificity regarding the mandatory fields and anonymous submission. Rewrite to clarify these details.

The original HLG includes registration and email confirmation, which are prerequisites for report submission but not part of the core 'submit report' functionality. The HLG's scope is too broad. It should focus on the submission process, including location tagging, description, category selection, and photo attachments, while keeping the registration requirements as a separate functional area.

The original HLG conflates Organization Office and Technical Office responsibilities. It should separate review/approval/rejection from assignment, status updates, and external company management.

The original HLG does not explicitly mention the possibility of written explanations for rejections. Rewrite to include this detail.

The original HLG conflates the responsibilities of the Organization Office Staff and the Technical Office Staff. The documentation specifies that the Organization Office performs preliminary review (approval/rejection), while the Technical Office is responsible for assigning reports and managing the lifecycle (status updates, external assignments). These distinct roles must be added to the functional boundaries of the/the HLG to reflect the correct actor responsibilities.

The original HLG misrepresents the scope: it should focus on public statistics visibility (including maps/tables) and anonymity display, not citizen exploration or data patterns.

The original HLG does not specify the public statistics' detailed features like filtering and sorting options. Rewrite to include these.

The original HLG incorrectly combines public statistics with the map and summary table views. The documentation states that the map and summary table are for viewing reports, and the public statistics section is a dedicated section for trends and categories. The HLG should be revised to focus on the public statistics functionality, removing the map and table views which are part of the report visibility and tracking functionality.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the detailed private statistics accessible to administrators. Rewrite to specify these.

The original HLG includes 'private statistics' as part of 'system settings' and 'external access' management. The documentation describes private statistics (charts and tables) as a separate functional area for strategic oversight, distinct from the configuration of system settings and management of external company access. The HLG should be split or revised to reflect these distinct functional boundaries.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are mostly aligned with the high-level goals and the software description, covering all key functionalities such as report submission, status tracking, notifications, review processes, external company management, and statistics. However, there is a minor omission regarding the automatic assignment of reports to external companies based on category configuration by the municipal administrator, which is mentioned in the high-level goal but not explicitly covered as a distinct low-level goal for the Municipal Administrator actor.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG lacks clarity on the distinction between managing report lifecycle states (In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended) and handling external company assignments. It should explicitly mention the ability to configure automatic assignment rules by administrators.

The original HLG is overly broad and does not clearly delineate the staff's responsibilities in assigning, updating statuses, or managing external company assignments. Rewrite to specify these duties.

The original HLG inadequately represents the full scope of the Technical Office Staff's responsibilities. It fails to mention the manual status update process for external companies without system access (Case 2), which is a document-confirmed requirement. The rewrite should preserve the manual update capability for external maintenance while maintaining the category-based assignment and status management functionality.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the distinction between managing report lifecycle states (In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended) and handling external company assignments. It should explicitly mention the ability to configure automatic assignment rules by administrators.

The original HLG incorrectly restricts public statistics access to citizens, while the documentation states non-registered users can view them. It should clarify that public statistics are accessible without registration.

The original HLG is overly broad and does not clearly delineate the staff's responsibilities in assigning, updating statuses, or managing external company assignments. Rewrite to specify these duties.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG omits the ability to manage external company assignments and does not explicitly mention the 'Suspended' state, which is critical for organizational workflows. The description should clarify that Technical Office Staff can update statuses (In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Resolved) and handle external assignments when configured by administrators.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the process for assigning reports to external companies. It should specify that this assignment is contingent upon prior administrator configuration.

The original HLG's description includes 'manage external company assignments', which is a configuration task for the Municipal Administrator (Section B, Case 1). Technical Office Staff manage the lifecycle and category-based assignment of reports, but the configuration of automatic assignment rules is a separate administrative function. The rewrite should focus on report lifecycle management and category-based assignment.

The original HLG omits the ability to manage external company assignments and does not explicitly mention the 'Suspended' state, which is critical for organizational workflows. The description should clarify that Technical Office Staff can update statuses (In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Resolved) and handle external assignments when configured by administrators.

The original HLG incorrectly restricts public statistics to non-registered users only, while the documentation states they are also visible to registered citizens. The description should clarify that public statistics are accessible to all users (registered and non-registered) without requiring registration.
The original HLG lacks clarity on the process for assigning reports to external companies. It should specify that this assignment is contingent upon prior administrator configuration.

The original HLG's description includes 'manage external company assignments', which is a configuration task for the Municipal Administrator (Section B, Case 1). Technical Office Staff manage the lifecycle and category-based assignment of reports, but the configuration of automatic assignment rules is a separate administrative function. The rewrite should focus on report lifecycle management and category-based assignment.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are comprehensive and align well with the high-level goals, covering all functional aspects of the Participium system. However, there is a minor omission regarding the automatic assignment of reports to external companies based on category configuration by administrators, which is mentioned in the description but not explicitly covered as a distinct low-level goal for the Municipal Administrator actor.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG suggests 'Configure System Settings and Manage External Access' which seems to encompass a broader scope than the reconstructed HLG, 'Enable Municipal Administrators to Govern Urban Issue Management'. The latter focuses more on strategic oversight rather than system configuration. Rewrite to align with the functional boundaries of other HLGs while preserving the core functionality.

The original HLG is too broad and includes 'view detailed private statistics' which is a distinct functionality from 'configure system settings and manage external access'. Furthermore, the documentation specifies that private statistics are only accessible to administrators, while the configuration and access management are core administrative tasks. The rewrite should focus on the administrative governance and configuration tasks, ensuring the private statistics are correctly categorized as a separate oversight function.

The original HLG inadequately represents the supported functionality by omitting 'interactive access' and 'filtered and sortable visualizations', which are explicitly documented. Rewrite to clarify these aspects while preserving all mandatory requirements.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG suggests 'Configure System Settings and Manage External Access' which seems to encompass a broader scope than the reconstructed HLG, 'Enable Municipal Administrators to Govern Urban Issue Management'. The latter focuses more on strategic oversight rather than detailed configuration. Rewrite to align with the functional boundaries of other HLGs while preserving the core functionality.

The original HLG lacks the specific requirement for private statistics. The HLG's description mentions 'strategic oversight' and 'configuration', but the documentation explicitly requires private statistics (charts and tables) accessible only to administrators, which is a distinct and important functionality for oversight. The rewrite should ensure these are included.

The original HLG's description incorrectly restricts public statistics to non-registered users only, while documentation confirms that public statistics are accessible to all, including registered citizens. The rewrite should clarify this and align with the documented functionality.

The latter focuses more on strategic oversight rather than detailed configuration. Rewrite to align with the functional boundaries of other HLGs while preserving the core functionality.

The rewrite should ensure these are included.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are comprehensive and align well with the high-level goals, covering all functional aspects of the software description. However, there is a minor omission regarding the automatic assignment of reports to external companies based on category configuration by the municipal administrator. This functionality is mentioned in the software description but not explicitly covered as a low-level goal for the Municipal Administrator actor.

feedback.critique:
Original HLG omits 'private access' and 'detailed private statistics', which are documented as core functionalities for administrators. Rewrite to clarify these aspects while preserving supported functionality.

The original HLG suggests a broad administrative role for the Municipal Administrator, which may not accurately reflect the detailed configuration and access management tasks. Rewrite to clarify specific responsibilities related to system settings, external company access, and private statistics.

The original HLG's description of 'private statistics' is slightly ambiguous regarding the specific content. The documentation specifies that private statistics are only accessible to administrators and include charts and tables in addition to public statistics. The rewrite should ensure it clearly covers configuration of system settings, management of external company access, and the comprehensive view of private statistics (including charts and tables) for strategic oversight.

feedback.critique:
Original HLG lacks specificity about 'private access' and 'detailed private statistics'. Clarify scope to include configuration, governance, and strategic monitoring as described in documentation.

The original HLG suggests 'Enable Municipal Administrators to Govern Urban Issue Management' which seems overly broad. Rewrite to clarify specific administrative functionalities like system configuration, external company access management, and detailed private statistics access for strategic oversight.

The original HLG's scope is too broad ('Govern Urban Issue Management'). The documentation specifies that the administrator's role is limited to configuring system settings, managing external company access, and viewing private statistics. The rewrite should focus on these specific administrative and oversight functions.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG omits the distinction between external companies with and without Participium access, which is critical for supported functionality. It also lacks clarity on private communication channels between technical office staff and external maintenance personnel.

The original HLG does not adequately represent the complexity of managing report assignments and private communications with external personnel. Rewrite to better capture these aspects while preserving functionality.

The original HLG inadequately represents the full scope of the Technical Office Staff's responsibilities. It fails to mention that they are responsible for manually moving reports to 'Resolved' state when external companies do not have system access (Case 2). This functionality is required by the user story and must be preserved.

The original HLG incorrectly restricts public statistics access to citizens, while documentation confirms non-registered users can view them. Clarify scope and remove the citizen-specific limitation.

The original HLG states that non-registered users can view public statistics, but it fails to mention that these statistics are also visible to non-registered users. Wait, the description says 'visible to non-registered users' twice. Actually, the problem is that the original HLG says 'including charts and tables', which are explicitly described in the documentation as being part of the PRIVATE section for administrators only. Public statistics should only include 'number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month'. Charts and tables are for the private section.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the extent of administrative control and data access. Rewrite to specify these aspects clearly.

The original HLG combines system configuration, access management, and private statistics into one goal. However, the documentation describes these as distinct functional areas. Furthermore, the original HLG fails to mention that the administrator's role in managing external companies is specifically for configuration of automatic assignment, which is a key part of the lifecycle management. The goal should be more precise regarding the scope of oversight.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG omits the requirement for private statistics access and detailed data analysis, which are critical for strategic oversight. The description should explicitly mention private charts, tables, and configuration capabilities to align with documented functionality.

The original HLG suggests 'Configure System Settings and Manage External Company Access' which seems to encompass a broader scope than the reconstructed goal. The rewritten HLG should focus on specific administrative tasks related to system configuration and external access management, ensuring clarity and precision in responsibilities.

The original HLG is too broad and includes private statistics, which are not a core management function but a reporting output. The HLG should focus on the configuration of system settings, management of external company access, and the oversight of the reporting process as described in the documentation.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are well-defined and align with the high-level goals, covering all functional aspects of the software description. However, there is a minor omission regarding the automatic assignment of reports to external companies based on category configuration by the municipal administrator. This functionality is mentioned in the software description but not explicitly covered as a low-level goal for the Municipal Administrator actor.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG omits the mandatory email alert configuration and the ability to follow other reports, which are documented requirements. Preserve real-time in-app notifications, email alerts (configurable), and report following functionality.

The original HLG is too broad; it should specifically mention 'real-time in-app notifications' and 'email alerts (configurable to disable)'.

The original HLG is too broad. It should focus on the notification and messaging system for citizens, specifically including the ability to receive updates for reports they follow, as well as the ability for municipal operators to send messages that can be received by external chatbots.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the mandatory written explanation for rejections and the 'Pending Approval' state management. Preserve review, approval/rejection, and justification requirements.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the process for providing written explanations for rejections.

The original HLG is missing the critical functionality of the Organization Office Staff's role in the preliminary review process, specifically the requirement that reports remain in 'Pending Approval' state until they are reviewed.

The original HLG does not explicitly cover status updates (In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Resolved) or private communication with external personnel. Preserve lifecycle management and private comment functionality.

The original HLG does not explicitly mention 'private comments (not visible to citizens)' for communication with external maintenance personnel.

The original HLG should be refined to explicitly include the management of external company assignments and the specific status updates (In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Resolved) that are managed by the Technical Office Staff, ensuring the functional boundaries of other actors are preserved.

The original HLG omits the private access to system settings and assignment rules. Preserve configuration of external company access, permissions, and reporting process oversight.

The original HLG should specify 'private access' for configuring system settings and managing external company access.

The original HLG is missing the specific functionality of the Municipal Administrator's role in configuring the assignment rules for reports, which is a key part of the system's configuration and management of external entities.

The original HLG lacks detail on visual (charts) and tabular private statistics for strategic analysis. Preserve detailed trend and performance metrics access.

The original HLG lacks detail on the specific 'charts and tables' for detailed analysis of report trends, categories, and performance metrics.

The original HLG should be refined to focus on the public and private statistics, specifically the private statistics for administrators, which include charts and tables for detailed analysis, as opposed to the public statistics which are accessible to non-registered users.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG omits the mandatory email alert configuration and the ability to follow other reports, which are documented requirements. The rewrite should clarify these aspects while preserving the core functionality of notifications.

The original HLG description is too broad. It should specify the real-time notification aspect and the ability to follow other reports.

The original HLG is slightly broader than the reconstructed HLG's focus on notifications. It should be clarified that the primary goal is to provide updates and notifications for both personal reports and followed reports, ensuring the functionality for following other citizens' reports is explicitly included as a core requirement.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the mandatory justification for rejections and the 'Pending Approval' state transition, which are critical per documentation. The rewrite should explicitly address these aspects.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the written explanation requirement for rejections and the possibility of automatic assignment to external companies.

The original HLG's description includes the 'Pending Approval' state, which is a status detail rather than a high-level goal. The goal should focus on the core functionality of reviewing, approving, or rejecting reports with mandatory justifications for rejections, as expressed in the documentation.

The original HLG does not fully capture the documented functionality of managing external company assignments, including automatic assignment rules and private communication. The rewrite should clarify these aspects.

The original HLG does not explicitly mention private comments for communication between technical office staff and external maintenance personnel.

The original HLG description includes 'manage external company assignments when configured by administrators' as a functional scope. However, the documentation specifies that automatic assignment is a configuration by the administrator, while the manual assignment by technical office staff is a core lifecycle management task. The HLG should be refined to focus on the management of the report lifecycle and communication with external personnel.

The original HLG omits the documented requirement for administrators to oversee assignment rules and access permissions. The rewrite should explicitly include these aspects.

The original HLG should specify the detailed configuration options available to municipal administrators.

The original HLG includes 'oversee the reporting process' which is not explicitly defined as a functional requirement in the documentation. The HLG should be focused on the configuration of system settings, management of external company access, and the definition of the assignment rules for external entities.

The original HLG lacks specificity regarding the 'private statistics' functionality, which includes charts and tables. The rewrite should clarify this aspect while preserving the core requirement.

The original HLG lacks detail on the specific performance metrics and detailed analysis available in private statistics.

The original HLG description includes 'performance metrics' which are not explicitly mentioned in the documentation. The HLG should be refined to focus on the provision of private statistics including charts and tables for detailed analysis of report trends and categories.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are comprehensive and align well with the high-level goals, covering all functional aspects of the system. However, there is a minor omission regarding the automatic assignment of reports to external companies when configured by the municipal administrator. While this is partially addressed in "Configure Automatic Assignment Rules for External Companies," it does not explicitly mention the bypassing of the initial review process for certain categories, which is a critical functional requirement.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG inadequately represents the full scope of Technical Office Staff responsibilities, particularly regarding external company assignments and private communication. It should explicitly mention handling both cases (with/without Participium access) and administrator configuration dependencies.

The original HLG does not adequately capture the full scope of Technical Office Staff's responsibilities, particularly their role in managing external company assignments and private communication with these entities.

The original HLG is missing the critical functionality of allowing external maintenance personnel to move reports from 'Assigned' to 'In Progress'. This is a key part of the report lifecycle described in the documentation. The rewrite should ensure that the staff can manage the full lifecycle, including these specific transitions and the private communication channel with external workers.

The original HLG fails to distinguish between system settings configuration and external company access management, which are separate responsibilities. It should explicitly cover both policy configuration and permission oversight.

The original HLG does not fully represent the Municipal Administrator's role in configuring system settings and managing external company access, including oversight of assignment rules.

The original HLG is too narrow. It fails to include the functionality for managing external company access and the configuration of assignment rules. The documentation specifies that administrators must be able to configure the system to automatically assign reports to external companies based on category, which is a key administrative function.

The original HLG inadequately represents the full scope of Technical Office Staff responsibilities, particularly regarding external company assignments and private communication. It should explicitly mention handling both cases (with/without Participium access) and administrator configuration dependencies.
The original HLG omits the distinction between public statistics (visible to non-registered users) and private charts/tables. It should clarify that public stats exclude detailed visual data.

The original HLG fails to distinguish between system settings configuration and external company access management, which are separate responsibilities. It should explicitly cover both policy configuration and permission oversight.

The original HLG does not adequately capture the full scope of Technical Office Staff's responsibilities, particularly their role in managing external company assignments and private communication with these entities.
The original HLG does not fully represent the Municipal Administrator's role in configuring system settings and managing external company access, including oversight of assignment rules.

The original HLG is missing the critical functionality of allowing external maintenance personnel to move reports from 'Assigned' to 'In Progress'. This is a key part of the report lifecycle described in the documentation. The rewrite should ensure that the staff can manage the full lifecycle, including these specific transitions and the private communication channel with external workers.

The original HLG is too narrow. It fails to include the functionality for managing external company access and the configuration of assignment rules. The documentation specifies that administrators must be able to configure the system to automatically assign reports to external companies based on category, which is a key administrative function.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are comprehensive and align well with the high-level goals, covering all functional aspects of the system. However, there is a minor omission regarding the automatic assignment of reports to external companies when configured by the municipal administrator. While this is partially addressed in "Configure Automatic Assignment Rules for External Companies," it does not explicitly mention the bypassing of the initial review process for certain categories, which is a critical functional requirement.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG omits the private communication aspect between Technical Office Staff and External Maintenance Personnel, which is critical for supported functionality. It should explicitly mention managing external company assignments when configured by administrators and allowing private comments not visible to citizens.

The original HLG does not adequately represent the full scope of Technical Office Staff's responsibilities, including private communication with external maintenance personnel and automatic assignment rules.

The original HLG is too broad. It should focus on the lifecycle management and status updates of reports, as the assignment of reports to external companies is a specific configuration-based rule managed by the administrator, while the communication with external personnel is a core lifecycle task.

The original HLG inadequately represents the Municipal Administrator's role by omitting the configuration of system settings. It should explicitly state that administrators configure system settings, manage external company access, and oversee assignment rules.

The original HLG does not fully capture the complexity of system configuration and external company management tasks assigned to Municipal Administrators.

The original HLG's description includes 'oversee the assignment rules', which is not explicitly supported by the documentation. The HLG should be refined to focus on configuring system settings and managing external company access and policies.

The original HLG omits the private communication aspect between Technical Office Staff and External Maintenance Personnel, which is critical for supported functionality. It should explicitly mention managing external company assignments when configured by administrators and allowing private comments not visible to citizens.

The original HLG incorrectly restricts public statistics access to non-registered users only, while documentation confirms it should also be accessible to registered citizens. It should clarify that public statistics are visible to both registered and non-registered users.

The original HLG inadequately represents the Municipal Administrator's role by omitting the configuration of system settings. It should explicitly state that administrators configure system settings, manage external company access, and oversee assignment rules.

The original HLG does not adequately represent the full scope of Technical Office Staff's responsibilities, including private communication with external maintenance personnel and automatic assignment rules.
The original HLG does not fully capture the complexity of system configuration and external company management tasks assigned to Municipal Administrators.

The original HLG is too broad. It should focus on the lifecycle management and status updates of reports, as the assignment of reports to external companies is a specific configuration-based rule managed by the administrator, while the communication with external personnel is a core lifecycle task.

The original HLG's description includes 'oversee the assignment rules', which is not explicitly supported by the documentation. The HLG should be refined to focus on configuring system settings and managing external company access and policies.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are comprehensive and align well with the high-level goals, covering all functional aspects of the system. However, there is a minor omission regarding the automatic assignment of reports to external companies when configured by the municipal administrator. While this is partially addressed in "Configure Automatic Assignment Rules for External Companies," it does not explicitly mention the bypassing of the initial review process for certain categories, which is a critical functional requirement.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG omits the requirement for private communication between technical office staff and external maintenance personnel, which is critical per project documentation. It also lacks clarity on automatic assignment rules configured by administrators.

The original HLG inadequately represents the scope of tasks for Technical Office Staff, including status updates and private communication with external personnel. Rewrite to clarify these responsibilities.

The original HLG is missing the specific functionality of allowing communication with external maintenance personnel via private comments, which is not visible to citizens. This is a core part of the lifecycle management described in the documentation.

The original HLG lacks specificity about 'overseeing assignment rules and access permissions,' which is a documented requirement for municipal administrators. It also omits the need to configure system settings.

The original HLG does not sufficiently emphasize the administrator's role in configuring access and assignment rules for external entities. Rewrite to highlight these strategic aspects.

The original HLG's scope is too narrow; it fails to include the configuration of assignment rules for external entities, which is a documented requirement for automatic assignment of reports.

The original HLG omits the requirement for private communication between technical office staff and external maintenance personnel, which is critical per project documentation. It also lacks clarity on automatic assignment rules configured by administrators.

The original HLG incorrectly restricts public statistics to non-registered users only, while the documentation states they are also visible to registered citizens. It also omits trends over day, week, or month.

The original HLG lacks specificity about 'overseeing assignment rules and access permissions,' which is a documented requirement for municipal administrators. It also omits the need to configure system settings.

The original HLG inadequately represents the scope of tasks for Technical Office Staff, including status updates and private communication with external personnel. Rewrite to clarify these responsibilities.
The original HLG does not sufficiently emphasize the administrator's role in configuring access and assignment rules for external entities. Rewrite to highlight these strategic aspects.

The original HLG is missing the specific functionality of allowing communication with external maintenance personnel via private comments, which is not visible to citizens. This is a core part of the lifecycle management described in the documentation.
The original HLG's scope is too narrow; it fails to include the configuration of assignment rules for external entities, which is a documented requirement for automatic assignment of reports.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are comprehensive and align well with the high-level goals, covering all functional aspects of the system. However, there is a minor omission regarding the automatic assignment of reports to external companies when configured by the municipal administrator. While this is partially addressed in "Configure Automatic Assignment Rules for External Companies," it does not explicitly mention the bypassing of the initial review process for certain categories, which is a critical functional requirement.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG inadequately represents the full scope of Technical Office Staff responsibilities, particularly regarding external company assignments and communication with maintenance personnel. It should explicitly mention private comments visibility rules and automatic assignment configurations.

The original HLG inadequately represents the scope of Technical Office Staff's responsibilities, including managing report lifecycle and private communication with external maintenance personnel.

The original HLG is missing the specific functionality of managing external company assignments, which is a key part of the Technical Office's responsibilities. The rewrite should include the ability to assign reports to external companies when configured by administrators.

The original HLG omits the private access aspect for administrators, which is critical. It should explicitly state that municipal administrators have private access to configure settings and manage external company permissions.

The original HLG does not fully capture the complexity of system configuration and external company management by Municipal Administrators.

The original HLG's description is too broad and doesn't specify the assignment rules and access permissions for external entities, which are documented as key responsibilities. The rewrite should be more specific to the configuration of external company report handling policies.

The original HLG inadequately represents the full scope of Technical Office Staff responsibilities, particularly regarding external company assignments and communication with maintenance personnel. It should explicitly mention private comments visibility rules and automatic assignment configurations.

The original HLG incorrectly restricts public statistics to non-registered users only, while documentation states they are also visible to registered citizens. It should clarify that all users can view public statistics without requiring registration.

The original HLG omits the private access aspect for administrators, which is critical. It should explicitly state that municipal administrators have private access to configure settings and manage external company permissions.
The original HLG inadequately represents the scope of Technical Office Staff's responsibilities, including managing report lifecycle and private communication with external maintenance personnel.
The original HLG does not fully capture the complexity of system configuration and external company management by Municipal Administrators.

The original HLG is missing the specific functionality of managing external company assignments, which is a key part of the Technical Office's responsibilities. The rewrite should include the ability to assign reports to external companies when configured by administrators.

The original HLG's description is too broad and doesn't specify the assignment rules and access permissions for external entities, which are documented as key responsibilities. The rewrite should be more specific to the configuration of external company report handling policies.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are comprehensive and align well with the high-level goals, covering all functional aspects of the system. However, there is a minor omission regarding the automatic assignment of reports to external companies when configured by the municipal administrator. While this is partially addressed in "Configure Automatic Assignment Rules for External Companies," it does not explicitly mention the bypassing of the initial review process for certain categories, which is a critical functional requirement.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG omits the requirement for private communication between Technical Office Staff and External Maintenance Personnel, which is critical per project documentation. It also lacks clarity on the automatic assignment feature when configured by administrators.

The original HLG does not adequately capture the full scope of Technical Office Staff's responsibilities, particularly their ability to communicate privately with external maintenance personnel.

The original HLG is missing the specific functionality of allowing communication with external maintenance personnel via private comments, which is not visible to citizens. This is a core part of the lifecycle management for external companies. The rewrite should ensure this private communication channel is explicitly included.

The original HLG misrepresents the Municipal Administrator's role by omitting the requirement for private access to system settings and external company management. It also lacks clarity on overseeing assignment rules.

The original HLG does not fully represent the Municipal Administrator's role in configuring system settings and managing external company access.

The original HLG's description is too broad and doesn't explicitly mention the specific configuration of assignment rules for external companies, which is a key requirement in the report lifecycle section. The rewrite should be updated to include the configuration of assignment rules and access permissions for external entities.

The original HLG omits the requirement for private communication between Technical Office Staff and External Maintenance Personnel, which is critical per project documentation. It also lacks clarity on the automatic assignment feature when configured by administrators.
The original HLG incorrectly restricts public statistics to non-registered users only, while the documentation states that public statistics are accessible to all, including registered citizens.

The original HLG misrepresents the Municipal Administrator's role by omitting the requirement for private access to system settings and external company management. It also lacks clarity on overseeing assignment rules.
The original HLG does not adequately capture the full scope of Technical Office Staff's responsibilities, particularly their ability to communicate privately with external maintenance personnel.
The original HLG does not fully represent the Municipal Administrator's role in configuring system settings and managing external company access.

The original HLG is missing the specific functionality of allowing communication with external maintenance personnel via private comments, which is not visible to citizens. This is a core part of the lifecycle management for external companies. The rewrite should ensure this private communication channel is explicitly included.

The original HLG's description is too broad and doesn't explicitly mention the specific configuration of assignment rules for external companies, which is a key requirement in the report lifecycle section. The rewrite should be updated to include the configuration of assignment rules and access permissions for external entities.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are comprehensive and align well with the high-level goals, covering all functional aspects of the system. However, there is a minor omission regarding the automatic assignment of reports to external companies when configured by the municipal administrator. The original HLG omits the ability to manage external company assignments and private communication with citizens, which is documented in the project description. The rewrite should clarify that Technical Office Staff can configure automatic assignment rules for external companies and handle private communications.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the process of report assignment to external companies. It should specify that this assignment is contingent upon prior administrator configuration and can bypass initial review by municipal staff.

The original HLG is missing the requirement for external chatbot integration for communication, which is a key functional boundary. The HLG's scope should be expanded to include the ability for external chatbots to interact with the platform's communication features, ensuring the system supports the required functionality of allowing external chatbots to send/receive messages.

The original HLG lacks specificity about managing external company access permissions. The rewrite should explicitly mention configuring access rules and overseeing permissions for external entities, as documented in the project description.

The original HLG does not explicitly mention the administrator's ability to configure automatic assignment rules for external companies based on report categories.

The original HLG's description is too narrow. It must be expanded to include the management of assignment rules for external companies, as documented in the report lifecycle section. The HLG should clearly state that administrators can configure the rules for automatic assignment of reports to external companies based on category.

The original HLG omits the ability to manage external company assignments and private communication with citizens, which is documented in the project description. The rewrite should clarify that Technical Office Staff can configure automatic assignment rules for external companies and handle private communications.

The original HLG incorrectly restricts public statistics to non-registered users only, while the documentation states that public statistics are accessible to all, including registered citizens. The rewrite should clarify this and remove the restriction.

The original HLG lacks specificity about managing external company access permissions. The rewrite should explicitly mention configuring access rules and overseeing permissions for external entities, as documented in the project description.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the process of report assignment to external companies. It should specify that this assignment is contingent upon prior administrator configuration and can bypass initial review by municipal staff.
The original HLG does not explicitly mention the administrator's ability to configure automatic assignment rules for external companies based on report categories.

The original HLG is missing the requirement for external chatbot integration for communication, which is a key functional boundary. The HLG's scope should be expanded to include the ability for external chatbots to interact with the platform's communication features, ensuring the system supports the required functionality of allowing external chatbots to send/receive messages.

The original HLG's description is too narrow. It must be expanded to include the management of assignment rules for external companies, as documented in the report lifecycle section. The HLG should clearly state that administrators can configure the rules for automatic assignment of reports to external companies based on category.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG omits the requirement for private communication between Technical Office Staff and External Maintenance Personnel, which is documented as a supported functionality. The description should explicitly mention this to align with the project documentation.

The original HLG does not adequately represent the full scope of Technical Office Staff responsibilities, particularly their ability to communicate privately with external maintenance personnel and manage report status transitions through defined lifecycle states.

The original HLG is missing the specific functionality of managing external company assignments, which is a key part of the Technical Office Staff's responsibilities. The rewrite should include the ability to assign reports to external companies when configured by administrators, as documented in Section B.

The original HLG does not clearly specify the requirement for municipal administrators to configure system settings, which is a documented functionality. The description should explicitly mention this to align with the project documentation.

The original HLG does not fully capture the breadth of Municipal Administrator responsibilities, especially their role in configuring system settings and managing external company access.

The original HLG description is too narrow; it should be expanded to include the management of assignment rules and access permissions for external entities, as specified in the project documentation (Section B). The reconstruction (HLG') reflects this broader scope.

The original HLG does not fully capture the breadth of Municipal Administrator responsibilities, especially their role in configuring system settings and managing external company access.

The original HLG is missing the specific functionality of managing external company assignments, which is a key part of the Technical Office Staff's responsibilities. The rewrite should include the ability to assign reports to external companies when configured by administrators, as documented in Section B.

The original HLG description is too narrow; it should be expanded to include the management of assignment rules and access permissions for external entities, as specified in the project documentation (Section B). The reconstruction (HLG') reflects this broader scope.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are mostly well-defined and align with the high-level goals, covering all necessary functional aspects of the system. However, there is a minor omission regarding the ability for citizens to disable email alerts in their user settings panel, which is mentioned in the software description but not explicitly covered as a low-level goal. Additionally, the functionality for external chatbots to send messages to citizens is implied but not directly addressed in the low-level goals.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG omits the mandatory email alerts (configurable to disable) and the ability for citizens to follow other reports, which are documented requirements. The rewrite should explicitly include these functionalities while preserving real-time in-app notifications.

The original HLG description is too broad. It should explicitly mention the real-time in-app notifications and email alerts for state changes, as well as the ability to follow other reports.

The original HLG is too narrow; it fails to mention that citizens can also receive messages from municipal operators and reply to them, which is a documented requirement. The rewrite should include the ability to receive and reply to messages from municipal staff.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the private communication channel with external maintenance personnel and the automatic assignment feature when configured by administrators. The rewrite should explicitly address these documented functionalities while preserving status management.

The original HLG description lacks clarity on the private communication between Technical Office Staff and external maintenance personnel, which should be explicitly stated.

The original HLG is incomplete. It must explicitly include the functionality for the technical office to manually move reports to 'Resolved' state when the external company does not have access to Participium (Case 2), as this is a key documented lifecycle management task.

The original HLG omits the private access to system settings configuration and oversight of assignment rules, which are documented requirements. The rewrite should explicitly include these functionalities while preserving external company access management.

The original HLG description should specify the private access for configuring system settings and managing external company access.

The original HLG description is missing the specific functionality to manage 'assignment rules' for external entities, which is a key part of the administrator's role in configuring system settings and managing external company access as described in the document.

The original HLG omits the mandatory email alerts (configurable to disable) and the ability for citizens to follow other reports, which are documented requirements. The rewrite should explicitly include these functionalities while preserving real-time in-app notifications.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the private communication channel with external maintenance personnel and the automatic assignment feature when configured by administrators. The rewrite should explicitly address these documented functionalities while preserving status management.

The original HLG incorrectly restricts public statistics to non-registered users only, while the documentation states they are also visible to registered citizens. The rewrite should clarify this and preserve the functionality for all user types.

The original HLG omits the private access to system settings configuration and oversight of assignment rules, which are documented requirements. The rewrite should explicitly include these functionalities while preserving external company access management.
The original HLG description is too broad. It should explicitly mention the real-time in-app notifications and email alerts for state changes, as well as the ability to follow other reports.
The original HLG description lacks clarity on the private communication between Technical Office Staff and external maintenance personnel, which should be explicitly stated.
The original HLG description should specify the private access for configuring system settings and managing external company access.

The original HLG is too narrow; it fails to mention that citizens can also receive messages from municipal operators and reply to them, which is a documented requirement. The rewrite should include the ability to receive and reply to messages from municipal staff.

The original HLG is incomplete. It must explicitly include the functionality for the technical office to manually move reports to 'Resolved' state when the external company does not have access to Participium (Case 2), as this is a key documented lifecycle management task.

The original HLG description is missing the specific functionality to manage 'assignment rules' for external entities, which is a key part of the administrator's role in configuring system settings and managing external company access as described in the document.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are mostly well-defined and align with the high-level goals, covering all necessary functional aspects of the system. However, there is a minor omission regarding the ability for citizens to disable email alerts in their user settings panel, which is mentioned in the software description but not explicitly covered as a low-level goal. Additionally, the functionality for external chatbots to send messages to citizens is implied but not directly addressed in the low-level goals.

feedback.critique:
Original HLG omits 'configurable email alerts' and 'following other reports', which are documented requirements. Rewrite to clarify these aspects while preserving core functionality.

The original HLG is too broad and does not clearly outline the real-time notification aspect. Rewrite to specify 'real-time in-app notifications and email alerts for every state change and messages exchanged with municipal staff.'

The original HLG is too broad. It should focus on the notification system for state changes and messages, while the 'follow other reports' functionality is a separate, distinct action for citizens. The reconstruction HLG' AI-generated text is more concise but doesn't capture the full scope of the original. The rewrite should clarify that notifications are triggered by state changes and messages, and citizens can follow other reports.

Original HLG lacks detail on 'private communication with external maintenance personnel' and 'automatic assignment rules'. Rewrite to reflect these documented functionalities.

The original HLG lacks clarity on private communication with external maintenance personnel. Rewrite to include 'private comments (not visible to citizens) for coordination between technical office staff and external maintenance workers.'

The original HLG is too broad. It should focus on the system's ability to manage the report lifecycle and assign reports to external companies. The reconstruction HLG' AI-generated text is more concise but doesn't capture the full scope of the original. The rewrite should clarify that the Technical Office Staff can manage the report lifecycle, assign reports to the user, and manage external company assignments.

Original HLG omits 'oversee assignment rules' and 'access permissions', which are documented. Rewrite to include these aspects while preserving core configuration functionality.

The original HLG is vague about the extent of configuration options. Rewrite to specify 'configure system settings, manage external company access, and oversee assignment rules and permissions for external entities.'

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are mostly well-defined and align with the high-level goals, covering all necessary functional aspects of the system. However, there is a minor omission regarding the ability for citizens to disable email alerts in their user settings panel, which is mentioned in the software description but not explicitly covered as a low-level goal. Additionally, the functionality for external chatbots to send messages to citizens is implied but not directly addressed in the low-level goals.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG omits the mandatory email alert configuration and the ability to follow other reports, which are documented requirements. The rewrite should clarify these aspects while preserving the core functionality of notifications.

The original HLG description is too broad. Rewrite to explicitly mention real-time in-app notifications and email alerts for state changes, as well as the ability to follow other reports.

The original HLG is too broad. It should focus on the notification system for state changes and messages, while the 'follow other reports' functionality is a separate, distinct requirement for social interaction. The documentation specifies that citizens can follow other reports, but this is a different functional boundary from the notification system itself.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the private communication aspect with external maintenance personnel and the automatic assignment rules. The rewrite should explicitly address these documented functionalities.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the private communication aspect between Technical Office Staff and external maintenance personnel.

The original HLG includes 'manage external company assignments' and 'private communication with external maintenance personnel'. While these are core tasks, the HLG's formulation is slightly imprecise regarding the scope of the technical office's role in the lifecycle management. The documentation specifies that the technical office manages the lifecycle and assigns reports, but the communication with external personnel is a specific, private interaction that should be clearly distinguished from the general lifecycle management.

The original HLG does not mention the private access to system settings and assignment rules, which are critical documented functionalities. The rewrite should include these aspects.

The original HLG does not sufficiently detail the configuration capabilities for municipal administrators.

The original HLG is too broad. It should focus on the configuration of system settings and management of external company access. The documentation specifies that the administrator's role is to configure system settings and manage external company access, and the assignment rules for external entities are part of this configuration. The HLG's formulation is slightly imprecise regarding the scope of the user's role in the oversight of external entities.

The original HLG omits the mandatory email alert configuration and the ability to follow other reports, which are documented requirements. The rewrite should clarify these aspects while preserving the core functionality of notifications.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the private communication aspect with external maintenance personnel and the automatic assignment rules. The rewrite should explicitly address these documented functionalities.

The original HLG incorrectly restricts public statistics to non-registered users only, while the documentation states they are also visible to registered citizens. The rewrite should reflect this inclusivity.
The original HLG does not mention the private access to system settings and assignment rules, which are critical documented functionalities. The rewrite should include these aspects.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG lacks clarity on the scope of notifications (real-time, in-app, email) and the ability to follow other reports. It should explicitly mention these aspects to align with documented functionality.

The original HLG description is too broad. It should specify the real-time notification aspect and the option to follow other reports for updates.

The original HLG is too narrow; it fails to include the requirement for external chatbots to access the notification and messaging functionality, which is a documented requirement in Section C.

The original HLG omits the distinction between public and private communication with external maintenance personnel. It should clarify that comments are not visible to citizens.

The original HLG description lacks clarity on the private communication aspect between Technical Office Staff and external maintenance personnel.

The original HLG fails to capture the specific functionality of manual status updates by technical office staff for reports where the external company does not have system access (Case 2 in Section B). It should be updated to include this manual resolution process.

The original HLG does not mention the private section for administrators or the ability to oversee assignment rules. It should explicitly include these aspects.

The original HLG description is vague. It should detail the specific settings and access management functionalities.

The original HLG is missing the specific functionality of overseeing assignment rules and access permissions for external entities, which is explicitly mentioned in Section B and the actor's description.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the scope of notifications (real-time, in-app, email) and the ability to follow other reports. It should explicitly mention these aspects to align with documented functionality.
The original HLG omits the distinction between public and private communication with external maintenance personnel. It should clarify that comments are not visible to citizens.
The original HLG incorrectly restricts public statistics to non-registered users only, while documentation states they are also visible to registered citizens. It should reflect this broader access.
The original HLG does not mention the private section for administrators or the ability to oversee assignment rules. It should explicitly include these aspects.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are comprehensive and align well with the high-level goals, covering all functional aspects of the software description. However, there is a minor omission regarding the citizen's ability to upload a personal photo in their user settings panel, which was mentioned in the software description under "CITIZEN UPDATES." Additionally, while the low-level goals cover most actions, they could be slightly more granular for some status updates (e.g., distinguishing between automatic and manual assignments for external companies). The inclusion of all actors' functionalities is thorough, but the missing personal photo upload feature should be addressed.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG omits the optional anonymity feature and lacks clarity on email notification configurability, which are documented in Section C. Preserve these aspects while refining the scope.

The original HLG is too narrow, focusing only on notifications. Rewrite to include broader aspects of transparency and trust-building, such as the ability for citizens to reply to municipal messages.

The original HLG lacks the specific functionality of external chatbot integration, which is a documented requirement for citizen updates. The rewrite should include the ability for external chatbots to access these notifications and messages.

The original HLG fails to mention mandatory written explanations for rejections (Section B) and the full state transition workflow. Clarify these requirements while maintaining the core review functionality.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the process for report rejection. Rewrite to include mandatory written explanations.

The original HLG does not capture the specific requirement of mandatory written explanations for rejections, which is a critical workflow step. The rewrite should ensure this mandatory documentation is included in the scope.
The original HLG omits the optional anonymity feature and lacks clarity on email notification configurability, which are documented in Section C. Preserve these aspects while refining the scope.

The original HLG fails to mention mandatory written explanations for rejections (Section B) and the full state transition workflow. Clarify these requirements while maintaining the core review functionality.
The original HLG is too narrow, focusing only on notifications. Rewrite to include broader aspects of transparency and trust-building, such as the ability for citizens to reply to municipal messages.
The original HLG lacks clarity on the process for report rejection. Rewrite to include mandatory written explanations.

The original HLG lacks the specific functionality of external chatbot integration, which is a documented requirement for citizen updates. The rewrite should include the ability for external chatbots to access these notifications and messages.

The original HLG is too narrow; it fails to mention the interactive map and summary table views, which are documented as the primary means for non-registered users to view statistics and trends. The rewrite should incorporate these specific UI components.

The original HLG does not capture the specific requirement of mandatory written explanations for rejections, which is a critical workflow step. The rewrite should ensure this mandatory documentation is included in the scope.

feedback.critique:
The original HLG omits the ability to configure automatic assignment of reports to external companies by category, which is a critical supported functionality. The description should explicitly include this feature to align with project documentation.

The original HLG does not adequately capture the administrative oversight aspect, including system configuration and external access management. Rewrite to: 'Enable municipal administrators to configure system settings, manage access for external maintenance companies, and view detailed private statistics for strategic operational oversight, including the ability to configure automatic assignment of reports to external companies by category.'

The original HLG's description includes 'view detailed private statistics', which is a distinct functionality from 'system configuration' and 'external access management'. The documentation specifies that private statistics are accessible only to administrators, but the HLG should clearly separate these distinct operational and analytical tasks to better reflect the functional boundaries of the system.

The original HLG inadequately represents the supported functionality by omitting details about automatic assignment for pre-configured categories and internal communication between technical staff and external maintenance personnel. The description should be expanded to include these aspects.

The original HLG lacks clarity on the mandatory written explanations for rejections. Rewrite to: 'Enable Organization Office Staff to review, approve, or reject citizen reports, with mandatory written explanations for rejections, and transition reports to the next state accordingly, ensuring accountability and transparency in the approval process.'

The original HLG's description is overly broad and conflates the management of report lifecycle states with the specific mechanism of 'automatic assignment' for pre-configured categories. The documentation specifies that automatic assignment is a configuration-led action by the administrator, while the technical office's role is primarily the manual assignment and management of reports. The HLG should be refined to focus on the report lifecycle management and internal communication.

The HLG should be refined to focus on the report lifecycle management and internal communication.
