feedback.critique:
For 'Enable Citizen Reporting with Location and Photo': the original HLG omits the requirement for anonymous reporting and email confirmation. Preserve location selection, form fields (title, description, category), photo attachments (up to 3), and ensure anonymous reporting is supported while verifying identity via email confirmation.

The original HLG 'Enable Citizen Reporting with Location and Photo' does not fully capture the requirement for email verification of citizens. Rewrite to include this essential step: 'Allow registered citizens to submit reports by selecting a location on the map, filling a form with mandatory fields (title, description, category), attaching one or more photos (up to 3) to document urban issues, and verifying their identity via email confirmation before submission.'

For 'Enable Citizen Reporting with Location and Photo': the HLG's description includes mandatory fields and photo limits, but the HLG' prime reveals that identity verification via email confirmation is a core part of the submission process. The rewrite should incorporate the requirement for email-confirmed registration before a citizen can submit a report.

For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Report Status': the original HLG excludes real-time notifications, email notifications, and platform messages with replies. Preserve all communication channels (in-app notifications, emails, platform messages) for status updates.

For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Report Status': the HLG' prime focuses on real-time notifications, while the original HLG description includes platform messages and replies. The rewrite should ensure that the functionality to send and receive messages (including replies) between municipal operators and citizens is explicitly preserved as a core communication channel.

For 'Ensure Efficient and Transparent Report Processing': the original HLG lacks clarity on structured workflow stages (approval, assignment, resolution). Clarify state transitions (Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected) and accountability.

For 'Ensure Efficient and Transparent Report Processing': the HLG' prime is too narrow, focusing only on the initiation of the workflow. The original HLG's description of a structured workflow with clear state transitions and accountability across multiple stages (approval, assignment, and resolution) must be preserved and reflected in the rewrite.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the original HLG omits secure internal communication channels. Preserve secure updates between technical offices and external personnel without exposing citizen data.

The original HLG 'Assign Reports to Technical Offices or External Companies Based on Category' lacks clarity regarding the secure communication channels between technical office staff and external maintenance personnel. Rewrite to include this detail: 'Enable Technical Office Staff to assign reports to the appropriate technical office or external maintenance company based on the problem category, ensuring correct routing and workflow continuity through secure internal communication channels for coordination without exposing citizen-facing data.'

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the HLG' prime is too narrow, focusing only on status updates. The original HLG's description of secure, internal communication channels (not visible to citizens) and status updates between technical office staff and external maintenance workers must be preserved.

For 'Provide Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics': the original HLG excludes interactive map views and filtering/sorting capabilities. Preserve public access with interactive visualizations, maps, summary tables, and filtering options.

For 'Provide Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics': the HLG' prime focuses on exploration, while the original HLG description includes specific views like interactive maps and summary tables with filtering and sorting. The rewrite should ensure these specific UI components and filtering capabilities are preserved.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the original HLG lacks detail on private statistics access. Preserve detailed visual/tabular analytics for administrators, including charts and tables.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the HLG' prime focuses on monitoring, while the original HLG description specifies private access to detailed visual and tabular statistics, including charts and tables. The rewrite should and ensure that the private nature of these statistics and the specific visual/tabular formats are preserved.

For 'Manage External Company Access and System Configuration': the original HLG omits automatic assignment rules. Preserve configuration of access and routing, including automatic assignment for specific categories.

For 'Manage External Company Access and System Configuration': the HLG' prime focuses on routing, while the original_hlg's description includes broader system configuration and granting/restricting access. The rewrite should ensure that the broader system configuration and access management for external companies are preserved.

feedback.critique:
For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Report Status': the original HLG incorrectly scopes notifications and messages to citizens only. Documentation confirms that municipal operators can also send messages, and external chatbots must be supported. Preserve all communication channels while ensuring they apply to both citizens and operators.

For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Report Status': the original HLG suggests real-time communication only through in-app notifications and platform messages. However, it should also include email updates and the ability to follow other citizens' reports with similar notification rules.

For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Report Status': the HLG's description includes 'the ability to follow other citizens’ open reports', which is a distinct functionality from the tracking of one's own reports. The documentation specifies that following other reports is a separate action. The HLG should be split or clarified to focus on the tracking of own reports and notifications, while preserving the ability to follow others.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the original HLG incorrectly assigns this to Technical Office Staff. Documentation confirms that Municipal Administrators configure access, while Technical Office Staff manage assignments. Correct the actor responsibility while preserving secure communication functionality.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the original HLG focuses on secure communication without specifying details about status updates. It should also include provisions for coordination without exposing citizen-facing data.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the HLG's description focuses on 'secure, internal communication channels', but the documentation highlights that the primary purpose is to allow staff and external maintainers to exchange information and comments that are not visible to citizens. The HLG should be rewritten to emphasize the exchange of information and comments for coordination, while preserving the secure, internal nature of the communication.

For 'Provide Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics': the original HLG incorrectly restricts access to registered users only. Documentation confirms that non-registered users can also view public statistics. Preserve all access levels while ensuring interactive visualizations and summary views are universally available.

For 'Provide Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics': the original HLG lacks detail on interactive visualizations and summary views. It should specify access for non-registered users and include trend visualizations over different time periods.

For 'Provide Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics': the HLG's description includes 'interactive map views, summary tables with filtering and sorting capabilities', which are actually part of the report viewing functionality (Section C). The statistics functionality (Section D) is specifically for trends over day, week, or month. The HLG should be rewritten to focus on the trends and visualizations of public statistics, removing the references to map views and summary tables.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the original HLG incorrectly scopes this to Municipal Administrators only. Documentation confirms that Technical Office Staff also need access to detailed statistics for monitoring trends. Correct the actor responsibility while preserving all analytical functionality.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the original HLG does not detail private analytics for monitoring trends and performance by category. It should specify access for municipal administrators and configuration options.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the HLG's description includes 'private access to detailed visual and tabular statistics', which is correct, but it also includes 'the ability to configure system settings and manage access for external companies'. These are two distinct functionalities: analytics and configuration. The HLG should be rewritten to focus on the administrative analytics, while the configuration and access management are covered by HLG 8.

For 'Manage External Company Access and System Configuration': the original HLG incorrectly assigns this solely to Municipal Administrators. Documentation confirms that Technical Office Staff also configure automatic assignment rules for specific categories. Correct the actor responsibility while preserving all configuration and access management functionality.

For 'Manage External Company Access and System Configuration': the HLG's description includes 'preserving broader system configuration and access management for external companies', which is slightly ambiguous. The documentation specifies that administrators can configure system settings, grant/restrict access, and configure automatic assignment rules. The HLG should be rewritten to clearly state these three specific administrative actions: configuration of settings, access management for external companies, and automatic assignment rules.

For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Report Status': the original HLG incorrectly scopes notifications and messages to citizens only. Documentation confirms that municipal operators can also send messages, and external chatbots must be supported. Preserve all communication channels while ensuring they apply to both citizens and operators.

Documentation separates these into distinct responsibilities: assignment is for routing, while secure communication is a separate workflow. Split the goal to reflect this separation.

feedback.critique:
For 'Ensure Efficient and Transparent Report Processing': the original HLG omits the requirement for justification in rejection cases, which is explicitly documented. Preserve the structured workflow while including mandatory written explanations for rejected reports.

For 'Ensure Efficient and Transparent Report Processing': the original HLG lacks clarity on how reports transition between stages. Rewrite to include specific state transitions (Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected) and accountability measures.

For 'Ensure Efficient and Transparent Report Processing': the original HLG is too broad and lacks the specific requirement for mandatory written explanations for rejected reports. The reconstruction HLG' ensure the lifecycle management and the mandatory rejection justification. Rewrite to include the mandatory written explanation for rejection to ensure transparency and accountability.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates': the original HLG incorrectly assigns this responsibility to Technical Office Staff. Documentation specifies that both Technical Office Staff and External Maintenance Personnel require secure communication channels for assigned reports.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the original HLG does not specify secure communication methods. Rewrite to include details on secure, internal channels for coordination without exposing citizen-facing data.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the original HLG focuses on communication channels, but the documentation specifies that external maintenance personnel can move reports from Assigned to In Progress and mark as resolved. The reconstruction HLG' captures this functional scope. Rewrite to include the ability for external maintainers to update report status (Assigned to In Progress, Resolved) and communicate internally without exposing citizen data.

For 'Provide Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics': the original HLG incorrectly restricts access to registered users. Documentation states that public statistics are visible to both non-registered and registered users.

For 'Provide Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics': the original HLG mentions trend visualizations, but the documentation specifies that public statistics concern the number of reports per category and trends over day, week, or month. The reconstruction HLG' captures this. Rewrite to ensure the public statistics include both the number of reports per category and the time-filtered trends.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the original HLG incorrectly assigns this responsibility only to municipal administrators. Documentation specifies that both Municipal Administrators and Technical Office Staff have access to private detailed statistics.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the original HLG lacks specificity on the nature of private statistics. Rewrite to detail visual and tabular representations for monitoring trends and performance by category.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the original HLG includes technical office staff in the scope of private statistics, but the documentation states that private statistics are accessible only to administrators. The reconstruction HLG' correctly identifies this restriction. Rewrite to restrict private statistics access to administrators only, while preserving the visual and tabular data for monitoring.

For 'Manage External Company Access and System Configuration': the original HLG incorrectly assigns this responsibility only to municipal administrators. Documentation specifies that both Municipal Administrators and Technical Office Staff are involved in configuring system settings, including external company access.

For 'Manage External Company Access and System Configuration': the original HLG includes technical office staff in the configuration of access and rules, but the documentation states that only the municipal administrator can configure system settings and manage access. The reconstruction HLG' correctly identifies this restriction. Rewrite to restrict configuration and access management to the municipal administrator only, while preserving the functionality to configure automatic assignment rules.

For 'Ensure Efficient and Transparent Report Processing': the original HLG omits the requirement for justification in rejection cases, which is explicitly documented. Preserve the structured workflow while including mandatory written explanations for rejected reports.

feedback.critique:
For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Report Status': the original HLG incorrectly scopes notifications and updates to real-time visibility, while documentation confirms these are event-driven (state changes) with multiple channels (in-app, email, platform messages). Preserve all notification types and channels, including replies from municipal operators and following other citizens' reports.

For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Report Status': the original HLG focuses on in-app notifications and platform messages. However, it does not explicitly mention email notifications or the ability to follow other citizens' reports. Rewrite to include these aspects while preserving real-time visibility into report status.

For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Report Status': the HLG's description includes 'the ability to follow other citizens’ open reports', which is a distinct functionality from the tracking of their own reports. The documentation specifies that following other reports is a separate action. The HLG should be split or rewritten to focus on the tracking of own reports to maintain functional boundaries.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the original HLG incorrectly broadens access to 'private' statistics, while documentation restricts detailed visual/tabular data strictly to administrators. Preserve private access and remove any implication of broader visibility.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the original HLG lacks specificity regarding the types of visual and tabular representations. Rewrite to detail these, ensuring administrators can monitor trends and performance by category.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the HLG's description focuses on 'visual and tabular statistics', but the documentation also emphasizes that administrators have private access to charts and tables for monitoring trends and performance. The HLG should be updated to explicitly include the monitoring of trends and performance to fully reflect the documented functionality.

For 'Manage External Company Access and System Configuration': the original HLG incorrectly assigns automatic assignment rules to external companies, while documentation confirms these are configured solely by municipal administrators. Preserve exclusive administrative control over access and routing.

For 'Manage External Company Access and System Configuration': the HLG's description mentions 'granting or restricting access' and 'configuring automatic assignment rules', which aligns with the documentation. However, the HLG's name is slightly less descriptive than the HLG'9s 'Manage system access and automated task routing'. The HLG should be rewritten to more clearly reflect the management of both system access and automated task routing for maintenance operations.

For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Report Status': the original HLG incorrectly scopes notifications and updates to real-time visibility, while documentation confirms these are event-driven (state changes) with multiple channels (in-app, email, platform messages). Preserve all notification types and channels, including replies from municipal operators and following other citizens' reports.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates': the original HLG omits the specific status transitions (Assigned → In Progress, Resolved) required for external maintenance personnel. Preserve secure communication while explicitly including these state updates.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the original HLG incorrectly broadens access to 'private' statistics, while documentation restricts detailed visual/tabular data strictly to administrators. Preserve private access and remove any implication of broader visibility.

For 'Manage External Company Access and System Configuration': the original HLG incorrectly assigns automatic assignment rules to external companies, while documentation confirms these are configured solely by municipal administrators. Preserve exclusive administrative control over access and routing.

For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Report Status': the original HLG focuses on in-app notifications and platform messages. However, it does not explicitly mention email notifications or the ability to follow other citizens' reports. Rewrite to include these aspects while preserving real-time visibility into report status.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the original HLG lacks specificity regarding the types of visual and tabular representations. Rewrite to detail these, ensuring administrators can monitor trends and performance by category.

For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Report Status': the HLG's description includes 'the ability to follow other citizens’ open reports', which is a distinct functionality from the tracking of their own reports. The documentation specifies that following other reports is a separate action. The HLG should be split or rewritten to focus on the tracking of own reports to maintain functional boundaries.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the HLG's description focuses on 'visual and tabular statistics', but the documentation also emphasizes that administrators have private access to charts and tables for monitoring trends and performance. The HLG should be updated to explicitly include the monitoring of trends and performance to fully reflect the documented functionality.

For 'Manage External Company Access and System Configuration': the HLG's description mentions 'granting or restricting access' and 'configuring automatic assignment rules', which aligns with the documentation. However, the HLG's name is slightly less descriptive than the HLG'9s 'Manage system access and automated task routing'. The HLG should be rewritten to more clearly reflect the management of both system access and automated task routing for maintenance operations.

feedback.critique:
For 'Enable Citizen Reporting with Location and Photo': the original HLG incorrectly restricts photo attachments to up to 3 per report, which is not a documented requirement. The description also inaccurately includes identity verification before submission, which is part of registration, not reporting. Preserve the core functionality of submitting reports with location, description, category, and optional photos while removing incorrect constraints.

The original HLG 'Enable Citizen Reporting with Location and Photo' does not fully capture the requirement for identity verification via email confirmation before submission. Rewrite to include this critical aspect of the reporting process.

For 'Enable Citizen Reporting with Location and Photo': the HLG's description includes 'verifying their identity via email confirmation before submission'. However, documentation states registration and email confirmation occur *before* a citizen can submit a report, not as a part of the submission process itself. Rewrite to clarify that registration is a prerequisite for submission, preserving the reporting functionality.

For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Own Report Status': the original HLG incorrectly includes the ability to follow other citizens' open reports, which is not a documented requirement for citizen tracking. The description also inaccurately restricts notifications to in-app and email, excluding platform messages with replies. Preserve real-time status updates through all documented channels while removing incorrect extensions.

For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Own Report Status': the HLG includes 'the ability to follow other citizens’ open reports'. While documentation supports this, the HLG's description of 'notifications' for following reports is tied to the same rules as their own reports. The HLG should be clarified to ensure it correctly reflects that following other reports is a distinct but related functionality, preserving all notification and messaging channels.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the original HLG incorrectly includes private access to detailed statistics, which is not a documented requirement. The description also inaccurately restricts access to administrators only, excluding other potential users. Preserve the core functionality of analyzing urban issue trends while removing incorrect constraints.

The original HLG 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making' lacks specificity regarding the detailed visual and tabular statistics provided to administrators. Rewrite to clearly outline these requirements.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the HLG's description mentions 'private access to detailed visual and tabular statistics'. Documentation confirms that private statistics are restricted to administrators and include charts and tables. However, the HLG's name is overly broad. It should be refined to focus specifically on the management of private statistics and performance monitoring, preserving the visual and tabular data access.

For 'Manage System Access and Automated Task Routing for External Maintenance Companies': the original HLG incorrectly restricts configuration and access management to the municipal administrator only, which is not a documented requirement. The description also inaccurately includes automated task routing, which is part of assignment rules, not system access. Preserve the core functionality of managing system access while removing incorrect extensions.

The original HLG 'Manage System Access and Automated Task Routing for External Maintenance Companies' does not specify the nature of automated task routing rules. Rewrite to include this detail, ensuring clarity on how these rules function.

For 'Manage System Access and Automated Task Routing for External Maintenance Companies': the HLG's description includes 'restricting configuration and access management to the municipal administrator only'. While documentation confirms this, the HLG's name is slightly imprecise. It should be refined to focus on the configuration of system settings and automated routing rules, preserving the administrator's exclusive access and the ability to configure external company access.

feedback.critique:
For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the original HLG inaccurately describes the functionality. Documentation confirms that administrators analyze urban issue trends, not strategic decision-making. Preserve trend analysis while removing references to strategic oversight.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the original HLG suggests detailed visual and tabular statistics for administrators. However, the description lacks clarity on what specific data or insights these statistics should provide. Rewrite to specify the types of visualizations (charts, graphs) and tabular representations (e.g., trend analysis over time by category), ensuring they support strategic decision-making.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the HLG's description includes 'visual and tabular statistics' and 'charts and tables', which are correctly identified in the documentation as being in the private section for administrators. However, the HLG's name is overly broad. The documentation specifies that this functionality is specifically for viewing private statistics. The rewrite should focus on 'Viewing Private Statistics' to better align with the documentation's specific functional scope.

For 'Manage System Access and Automated Task Routing for External Maintenance Companies': the original HLG incorrectly includes automated task routing, which is not documented. Preserve access management while removing references to workflow automation.

For 'Manage System Access and Automated Task Routing for External Maintenance Companies': the original HLG is broad. Rewrite to detail specific access configurations (e.g., read-only, full control) and automated task routing rules (e.g., automatic assignment based on category, time-based triggers), ensuring they align with maintenance operational needs without compromising security.

feedback.critique:
For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Own Report Status': the original HLG omits external chatbot support and focuses only on citizen visibility. Preserve real-time notifications, email alerts, platform messaging with replies, and following other citizens' reports while expanding to include external chatbot interactions as documented.

For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Own Report Status': the original HLG focuses on in-app notifications and platform messages. However, it should also include email notifications and the ability for citizens to follow other users' reports with the same notification rules.

For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Own Report Status': the HLG' is missing the requirement for external chatbots to interact with users or operators through the platform. The documentation specifies that the system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots. Preserve the notification and messaging rules while including chatbot accessibility.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the original HLG incorrectly restricts status updates to external maintainers only. Preserve secure internal communication for both technical offices and external personnel, ensuring they can update report status (Assigned to In Progress, Resolved) without exposing citizen data.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the original HLG lacks explicit mention of secure internal communication channels. It should be revised to include this aspect.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the HLG' is too narrow, only mentioning status changes. The documentation requires that staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, which are not visible to the reporting citizen. Preserve the internal communication and status update functionality.

For 'Provide Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics': the original HLG misrepresents the actor. Citizens do not analyze trends; public statistics are visible to all users, including non-registered ones. Correct the description to reflect that both registered and non-registered users view public statistics on report trends and categories.

For 'Provide Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics': the HLG' is missing the requirement for non-registered users to view public statistics. The documentation states that public statistics are visible to non-registered users. Preserve the trend and category analysis while ensuring access for both registered and non-registered users.

For 'Viewing Private Statistics': the original HLG omits the visual and tabular representations. Preserve detailed charts and tables for administrators while restricting access exclusively to them, ensuring full coverage of private statistics functionality.

For 'Provide Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics': the original HLG does not specify that non-registered users can also view these statistics. It should be updated to reflect this.

For 'Viewing Private Statistics': the HLG' is missing the requirement for administrators to view charts and tables in addition to the public statistics. The documentation specifies that in the private section, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables. Preserve the visual and tabular representations while ensuring they are viewed in addition to the public statistics.

For 'Managing System Settings and Access': the original HLG incorrectly restricts automatic assignment rules. Preserve configuration of system settings, access control for external companies, and workflow automation (e.g., automatic category assignments) as documented.

For 'Managing System Settings and Access': the HLG' is missing the requirement to configure automatic assignment rules for specific categories. The documentation specifies that automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator. Preserve the configuration of access and settings while including the automatic assignment rules.

For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Own Report Status': the original HLG omits external chatbot support and focuses only on citizen visibility. Preserve real-time notifications, email alerts, platform messaging with replies, and following other citizens' reports while expanding to include external chatbot interactions as documented.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the original HLG incorrectly restricts status updates to external maintainers only. Preserve secure internal communication for both technical offices and external personnel, ensuring they can update report status (Assigned to In Progress, Resolved) without exposing citizen data.

For 'Provide Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics': the original HLG misrepresents the actor. Citizens do not analyze trends; public statistics are visible to all users, including non-registered ones. Correct the description to reflect that both registered and non-registered users view public statistics on report trends and categories.

For 'Viewing Private Statistics': the original HLG omits the visual and tabular representations. Preserve detailed charts and tables for administrators while restricting access exclusively to them, ensuring full coverage of private statistics functionality.

For 'Managing System Settings and Access': the original HLG incorrectly restricts automatic assignment rules. Preserve configuration of system settings, access control for external companies, and workflow automation (e.g., automatic category assignments) as documented.

For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Own Report Status': the original HLG focuses on in-app notifications and platform messages. However, it should also include email notifications and the ability for citizens to follow other users' reports with the same notification rules.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the original HLG lacks explicit mention of secure internal communication channels. It should be revised to include this aspect.
For 'Provide Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics': the original HLG does not specify that non-registered users can also view these statistics. It should be updated to reflect this.

For 'Enable Citizen Tracking of Own Report Status': the HLG' is missing the requirement for external chatbots to interact with users or operators through the platform. The documentation specifies that the system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots. Preserve the notification and messaging rules while including chatbot accessibility.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the HLG' is too narrow, only mentioning status changes. The documentation requires that staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, which are not visible to the reporting citizen. Preserve the internal communication and status update functionality.

For 'Provide Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics': the HLG' is missing the requirement for non-registered users to view public statistics. The documentation states that public statistics are visible to non-registered users. Preserve the trend and category analysis while ensuring access for both registered and non-registered users.

For 'Viewing Private Statistics': the HLG' is missing the requirement for administrators to view charts and tables in addition to the public statistics. The documentation specifies that in the private section, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables. Preserve the visual and tabular representations while ensuring they are viewed in addition to the public statistics.

For 'Managing System Settings and Access': the HLG' is missing the requirement to configure automatic assignment rules for specific categories. The documentation specifies that automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator. Preserve the configuration of access and settings while including the automatic assignment rules.

feedback.critique:
For 'Assign Reports to Technical Offices or External Companies Based on Category': the original HLG omits secure internal communication channels and status updates between technical offices and external maintenance personnel, which are required for coordination. Preserve assignment functionality while including secure communication and status update capabilities.

For 'Assign Reports to Technical Offices or External Companies Based on Category': the original HLG suggests assigning reports based on category, but it lacks clarity on how external companies are involved. Rewrite to include explicit details about secure internal communication channels and status updates between technical office staff and external maintenance personnel.

For 'Assign Reports to Technical Offices or External Companies Based on Category': the HLG's description includes 'ensuring correct routing and workflow continuity through secure internal communication channels'. However, the documentation specifies that communication between technical offices and external companies is a separate functionality (Case 1 and Case 2 in Report Lifecycle). The HLG should be rewritten to focus solely on the assignment of reports based on category, preserving the routing and assignment logic.

feedback.critique:

For 'Provide Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics': the HLG's description mentions 'number of reports per category and trends over day, week, or month'. The documentation confirms this is the correct scope for public statistics. However, the HLG's name is slightly less descriptive than the reconstruction. The HLG should be rewritten to include 'analyzing' trends to better reflect the user's goal of understanding urban issues, while preserving the category and time-based trends.

For 'Viewing Private Statistics': the original HLG omits detailed visual and tabular statistics, which are required for municipal administrators. Preserve private statistics viewing while including charts and tables.

The HLG should be rewritten to focus on the analysis of trends and performance, ensuring the 'charts and tables' functionality is preserved while the name is updated to reflect the analysis goal.

feedback.critique:
For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the original HLG incorrectly assigns this functionality to Technical Office Staff. Documentation confirms that both Technical Office Staff and External Maintenance Personnel must handle secure communication, status updates, and coordination for assigned reports without exposing citizen data.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the original HLG does not adequately represent the secure, internal communication channels and status updates required between technical office staff and external maintenance personnel. Rewrite to include these specific functionalities while preserving the core objective of coordinating report resolution without exposing citizen data.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the HLG's scope is correctly aligned with the documentation, but the HLG'prime indicates a broader scope of 'tracking report lifecycle status' which is already covered by the general lifecycle management. The HLG should be refined to focus specifically on the private communication and status updates between technical and external staff, ensuring it doesn't overlap with the general lifecycle management. Preserve the private communication and status updates functionality.

For 'Manage System Access and Assignment Policies': the original HLG incorrectly restricts configuration and access management to Municipal Administrators only. Documentation confirms that Technical Office Staff must also be able to configure automatic assignment rules for specific categories, while restricting external maintenance company access.

For 'Manage System Access and Assignment Policies': the HLG'prime suggests a broader scope of 'managing external maintenance company access and assignment policies' which is more general than the specific configuration of system settings, access, and automatic assignment rules described in the documentation. The HLG should be refined to focus specifically on the configuration of system settings, access, and automatic assignment rules. Preserve the configuration of system settings, access, and and automatic assignment rules.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the original HLG incorrectly assigns this functionality to Technical Office Staff. Documentation confirms that both Technical Office Staff and External Maintenance Personnel must handle secure communication, status updates, and coordination for assigned reports without exposing citizen data.

For 'Manage System Access and Assignment Policies': the original HLG incorrectly restricts configuration and access management to Municipal Administrators only. Documentation confirms that Technical Office Staff must also be able to configure automatic assignment rules for specific categories, while restricting external maintenance company access.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the original HLG does not adequately represent the secure, internal communication channels and status updates required between technical office staff and external maintenance personnel. Rewrite to include these specific functionalities while preserving the core objective of coordinating report resolution without exposing citizen data.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the HLG's scope is correctly aligned with the documentation, but the HLG'prime indicates a broader scope of 'tracking report lifecycle status' which is already covered by the general lifecycle management. The HLG should be refined to focus specifically on the private communication and status updates between technical and external staff, ensuring it doesn't overlap with the general lifecycle management. Preserve the private communication and status updates functionality.

For 'Provide Public Access to Urban Issue Statistics': the HLG'prime suggests a broader scope of 'providing public access to report data' which includes more than just statistics. The HLG should be refined to focus specifically on the proposed public statistics (number of reports per category, trends over day, week, or month) as described in the documentation. Preserve the public statistics functionality.

For 'Analyze Urban Issue Trends Through Private Statistics': the HLG'prime suggests a broader scope of 'monitoring urban issue trends and performance metrics' which is more general than the specific private statistics (charts and tables) described in the documentation. The HLG should be refined to focus specifically on the private statistics for administrators. Preserve the private statistics functionality.

For 'Manage System Access and Assignment Policies': the HLG'prime suggests a broader scope of 'managing external maintenance company access and assignment policies' which is more general than the specific configuration of system settings, access, and automatic assignment rules described in the documentation. The HLG should be refined to focus specifically on the configuration of system settings, access, and automatic assignment rules. Preserve the configuration of system settings, access, and and automatic assignment rules.

However, there is a minor omission regarding the "Suspended" state for reports, which is mentioned in the description but not explicitly covered as a low-level goal for the Organization Office Staff or Technical Office Staff. Additionally, the low-level goal for the citizen receiving a mandatory email confirmation after registration is associated with the wrong high-level goal (it should be related to user management rather than reporting). The rest of the goals are well-defined and cover all necessary functionalities.

feedback.critique:
For 'Assign Reports to Technical Offices or External Companies Based on Category': the original HLG focuses solely on assignment, omitting lifecycle management (e.g., state transitions). Preserve assignment functionality while expanding scope to include full report lifecycle management from assignment to resolution.

For 'Assign Reports to Technical Offices or External Companies Based on Category': the original HLG suggests assignment based on category, but it lacks clarity on how external companies are involved. Rewrite to include explicit details about the process of assigning reports to external maintenance personnel when necessary.

For 'Assign Reports to Technical Offices or External Companies Based on Category': the HLG's scope is too narrow. Documentation specifies that Technical Office Staff are responsible for managing the report lifecycle from assignment to resolution, including moving reports to 'Work in Progress', 'Suspended', and 'Final' states. The HLG's focus on assignment alone fails to capture the full lifecycle management responsibility. Rewrite to include the full lifecycle management of reports.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the original HLG incorrectly broadens functionality beyond private comments, including status updates (e.g., Assigned to In Progress). Restrict scope to secure internal communication only, preserving private comment functionality.

For 'Support Secure Internal Communication and Status Updates Between Technical Offices and External Maintenance Personnel': the HLG's description is well-aligned with the documentation. However, the HLG'prime's focus on 'private comments' is a subset of the functionality. The original HLG correctly captures the secure internal communication, status updates (Assigned to In Progress, Resolved), and coordination without exposing citizen data. No rewrite is required as the original HLG is more comprehensive than the reconstruction.

For 'Manage System Access and Assignment Policies': the original HLG incorrectly includes automatic assignment rules, which are part of report processing (HLG 3). Restrict scope to access management only, preserving external company access configuration while excluding assignment policies.

For 'Manage System Access and Assignment Policies': the original HLG is broad and could benefit from more specific details about how municipal administrators configure access for external companies and set up automatic assignment rules. Rewrite to include these specifics, ensuring all functionalities are clearly outlined.

For 'Manage System Access and Assignment Policies': the HLG's description is well-aligned with the documentation. However, the HLG'prime's focus on 'restricted administrative control' is a subset of the functionality. The original HLG correctly captures the system settings configuration, external company access management, and automatic assignment rules. No rewrite is required as the original HLG is more comprehensive than the reconstruction.

For 'Assign Reports to Technical Offices or External Companies Based on Category': the original HLG focuses solely on assignment, omitting lifecycle management (e.g., state transitions). Preserve assignment functionality while expanding scope to include full report lifecycle management from assignment to resolution.

For 'Assign Reports to Technical Offices or External Companies Based on Category': the original HLG suggests assignment based on category, but it lacks clarity on how external companies are involved. Rewrite to include explicit details about the process of assigning reports to external maintenance personnel when necessary.

For 'Manage System Access and Assignment Policies': the original HLG is broad and could benefit from more specific details about how municipal administrators configure access for external companies and set up automatic assignment rules. Rewrite to include these specifics, ensuring all functionalities are clearly outlined.

Documentation specifies that Technical Office Staff are responsible for managing the report lifecycle from assignment to resolution, including moving reports to 'Work in Progress', 'Suspended', and 'Final' states. lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are well-defined, functional, and align with the high-level goals. They cover all necessary actions for each actor without any contradictions or omissions. However, there is a minor issue: the "Organization Staff transitions report to In Progress" goal seems redundant because it overlaps with the "Technical Staff transitions report to Work in Progress" goal, which already covers the state transition after approval. Additionally, the description of some low-level goals could be more precise (e.g., "Organization Staff transitions report to Pending Approval" lacks clarity on when this happens). The system's description is fully represented, and no major improvements are needed.

feedback.critique:
For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the original HLG incorrectly restricts configuration to municipal administrators only, while documentation allows automatic assignment rules for specific categories by municipal administrators. Preserve the ability to configure access and assignment rules while ensuring proper restrictions.

For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the original HLG suggests restricting configuration and access management to municipal administrators only. However, the description implies broader functionalities including setting up automatic assignment rules for specific categories. Rewrite to clarify that these rules can be configured by the administrator but executed automatically under certain conditions, ensuring clarity on system behavior.

For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the HLG's description includes 'restricting configuration and access management to the municipal administrator only', which is already a fundamental property of the actor's role and not a specific functional requirement. Furthermore, the HLG's name and description are slightly broader than the reconstruction. The rewrite should focus on the core functionality of configuring access for external companies and setting up automatic assignment rules for specific categories, as confirmed by the documentation.

For 'Manage Full Report Lifecycle from Assignment to Resolution': the original HLG incorrectly includes state transitions (Assigned, Work in Progress, Suspended, Resolved) that are not part of the supported lifecycle. The documented states are Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. Preserve only the supported transitions and remove unsupported ones.

For 'Analyze Urban Issue Trends Through Private Statistics': the original HLG incorrectly includes public statistics visibility. The documented private statistics are accessible only to administrators and include detailed visual and tabular data, excluding public trends. Preserve private statistics and remove public visibility.

For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the original HLG incorrectly restricts configuration to municipal administrators only, while documentation allows automatic assignment rules for specific categories by municipal administrators. Preserve the ability to configure access and assignment rules while ensuring proper restrictions.

For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the original HLG suggests restricting configuration and access management to municipal administrators only. However, the description implies broader functionalities including setting up automatic assignment rules for specific categories. Rewrite to clarify that these rules can be configured by the administrator but executed automatically under certain conditions, ensuring clarity on system behavior.

For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the HLG's description includes 'restricting configuration and access management to the municipal administrator only', which is already a fundamental property of the actor's role and not a specific functional requirement. Furthermore, the HLG's name and description are slightly broader than the reconstruction. The rewrite should focus on the core functionality of configuring access for external companies and setting up automatic assignment rules for specific categories, as confirmed by the documentation.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are mostly well-defined and align with the high-level goals, covering all major functionalities described in the software description. However, there is a critical omission: the high-level goal "Analyze Urban Issue Trends Through Public Transparency" (referenced in the last low-level goal) does not exist in the provided high-level goals list. This suggests an inconsistency where a low-level goal references a non-existent high-level goal. Additionally, while the low-level goals cover most aspects of report submission, lifecycle management, and communication, there is no explicit mention of the mandatory written explanation for rejected reports (as described in section B). The functionality for external chatbots interacting with citizens is also not fully addressed in the low-level goals, as it only mentions "Citizen interacts with external chatbot for report status" without detailing how this works from the technical office or administrator side. Lastly, the low-level goal for non-registered users viewing public statistics introduces a new actor ("Non-registered user") that was not listed in the actors section.

feedback.critique:
For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the original HLG incorrectly restricts configuration to municipal administrators only, while documentation allows automatic assignment rules for specific categories by municipal administrators. Preserve the ability to configure access and assignment rules while ensuring proper restrictions.

For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the original HLG suggests restricting configuration and access management to municipal administrators only. However, the description implies broader functionalities including setting up automatic assignment rules for specific categories. Rewrite to clarify that these rules can be configured by the administrator but executed automatically under certain conditions, ensuring clarity on system behavior.

For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the HLG's description includes 'restricting configuration and access management to the municipal administrator only', which is already a fundamental property of the actor's role and not a specific functional requirement. Furthermore, the HLG's name and description are slightly broader than the reconstruction. The rewrite should focus on the core functionality of configuring access for external companies and setting up automatic assignment rules for specific categories, as confirmed by the documentation.

For 'Manage Full Report Lifecycle from Assignment to Resolution': the original HLG incorrectly includes state transitions (Assigned, Work in Progress, Suspended, Resolved) that are not part of the supported lifecycle. The documented states are Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. Preserve only the supported transitions and remove unsupported ones.

For 'Analyze Urban Issue Trends Through Private Statistics': the original HLG incorrectly includes public statistics visibility. The documented private statistics are accessible only to administrators and include detailed visual and tabular data, excluding public trends. Preserve private statistics and remove public visibility.

For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the original HLG incorrectly restricts configuration to municipal administrators only, while documentation allows automatic assignment rules for specific categories by municipal administrators. Preserve the ability to configure access and assignment rules while ensuring proper restrictions.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are mostly well-defined and align with the high-level goals, covering all major functionalities described in the software description. However, there is a critical omission: the high-level goal "Analyze Urban Issue Trends Through Public Transparency" (referenced in the last low-level goal) does not exist in the provided high-level goals list. This suggests an inconsistency where a low-level goal references a non-existent high-level goal. Additionally, while the low-level goals cover most aspects of report submission, lifecycle management, and communication, there is no explicit mention of the mandatory written explanation for rejected reports (as described in section B). The functionality for external chatbots interacting with citizens is also not fully addressed in the low-level goals, as it only mentions "Citizen interacts with external chatbot for report status" without detailing how this works from the technical office or administrator side. Lastly, the low-level goal for non-registered users viewing public statistics introduces a new actor ("Non-registered user") that was not listed in the actors section.

feedback.critique:
For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the original HLG incorrectly restricts configuration to municipal administrators only, while documentation allows automatic assignment rules for specific categories by municipal administrators. Preserve the ability to configure access and assignment rules while ensuring proper restrictions.

For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the original HLG suggests restricting configuration and access management to municipal administrators only. However, the description implies broader functionalities including setting up automatic assignment rules for specific categories. Rewrite to clarify that these rules can be configured by the administrator but executed automatically under certain conditions, ensuring clarity on system behavior.

For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the HLG's description includes 'restricting configuration and access management to the municipal administrator only', which is already a fundamental property of the actor's role and not a specific functional requirement. Furthermore, the HLG's name and description are slightly broader than the reconstruction. The rewrite should focus on the core functionality of configuring access for external companies and setting up automatic assignment rules for specific categories, as confirmed by the documentation.

For 'Manage Full Report Lifecycle from Assignment to Resolution': the original HLG incorrectly includes state transitions (Assigned, Work in Progress, Suspended, Resolved) that are not part of the supported lifecycle. The documented states are Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. Preserve only the supported transitions and remove unsupported ones.

For 'Analyze Urban Issue Trends Through Private Statistics': the original HLG incorrectly includes public statistics visibility. The documented private statistics are accessible only to administrators and include detailed visual and tabular data, excluding public trends. Preserve private statistics and remove public visibility.

For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the original HLG incorrectly restricts configuration to municipal administrators only, while documentation allows automatic assignment rules for specific categories by municipal administrators. Preserve the ability to configure access and assignment rules while ensuring proper restrictions.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are mostly well-defined and align with the high-level goals, covering all major functionalities described in the software description. However, there is a critical omission: the high-level goal "Analyze Urban Issue Trends Through Public Transparency" (referenced in the last low-level goal) does not exist in the provided high-level goals list. This suggests an inconsistency where a low-level goal references a non-existent high-level goal. Additionally, while the low-level goals cover most aspects of report submission, lifecycle management, and communication, there is no explicit mention of the mandatory written explanation for rejected reports (as described in section B). The functionality for external chatbots interacting with citizens is also not fully addressed in the low-level goals, as it only mentions "Citizen interacts with external chatbot for report status" without detailing how this works from the technical office or administrator side. Lastly, the low-level goal for non-registered users viewing public statistics introduces a new actor ("Non-registered user") that was not listed in the actors section.

feedback.critique:
For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the original HLG incorrectly restricts configuration to municipal administrators only, while documentation allows automatic assignment rules for specific categories by municipal administrators. Preserve the ability to configure access and assignment rules while ensuring proper restrictions.

For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the original HLG suggests restricting configuration and access management to municipal administrators only. However, the description implies broader functionalities including setting up automatic assignment rules for specific categories. Rewrite to clarify that these rules can be configured by the administrator but executed automatically under certain conditions, ensuring clarity on system behavior.

For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the HLG's description includes 'restricting configuration and access management to the municipal administrator only', which is already a fundamental property of the actor's role and not a specific functional requirement. Furthermore, the HLG's name and description are slightly broader than the reconstruction. The rewrite should focus on the core functionality of configuring access for external companies and setting up automatic assignment rules for specific categories, as confirmed by the documentation.

For 'Manage Full Report Lifecycle from Assignment to Resolution': the original HLG incorrectly includes state transitions (Assigned, Work in Progress, Suspended, Resolved) that are not part of the supported lifecycle. The documented states are Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. Preserve only the supported transitions and remove unsupported ones.

For 'Analyze Urban Issue Trends Through Private Statistics': the original HLG incorrectly includes public statistics visibility. The documented private statistics are accessible only to administrators and include detailed visual and tabular data, excluding public trends. Preserve private statistics and remove public visibility.

For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the original HLG incorrectly restricts configuration to municipal administrators only, while documentation allows automatic assignment rules for specific categories by municipal administrators. Preserve the ability to configure access and assignment rules while ensuring proper restrictions.

However, the description implies broader functionalities including setting up automatic assignment rules for specific categories. feedback.critique:
For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the original HLG includes automatic assignment rules, which is not documented. Preserve configuration of access but remove automatic assignment to align with municipal administrator's exclusive control.

For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the original HLG suggests restricting configuration and access management to municipal administrators only. However, the description implies broader functionalities including setting up automatic assignment rules for specific categories. Rewrite to clarify that these rules can be configured by the administrator but executed automatically under certain conditions, ensuring clarity on system behavior.

For 'Manage System Access and External Company Integration Policies': the HLG's description includes 'restricting configuration and access management to the municipal administrator only', which is already a fundamental property of the actor's role and not a specific functional requirement. Furthermore, the HLG's name and description are slightly broader than the reconstruction. The rewrite should focus on the core functionality of configuring access for external companies and setting up automatic assignment rules for specific categories, as confirmed by the documentation.

However, there is a minor issue: the low-level goal "Organization Staff transitions report to In Progress" should logically follow after approval (i.e., it should be transitioned from "Pending Approval" to "In Progress"). The current description implies that the Organization Office Staff sets the state directly to "In Progress," which may not accurately reflect the workflow described in the software description. Additionally, the low-level goal "Technical Staff transitions report to Work in Progress" is redundant because it should be transitioned from "Assigned" to "Work in Progress," and this action is already covered by the high-level goal.

feedback.critique:
For 'Enable Citizen Participation in Urban Management': the original HLG overstates functionality by including tracking and transparency, which are not explicitly required. The documented scope is limited to reporting issues with location/photo and status updates. Preserve reporting while removing tracking and transparency claims.

For 'Enable Citizen Participation in Urban Management': The original HLG is too broad. It should explicitly mention reporting issues with location and photo, as well as tracking report status to foster transparency and civic engagement.

For 'Enable Citizen Participation in Urban Management': the HLG's description includes 'foster transparency and civic engagement', which are high-level objectives rather than specific functionalities. The HLG'prime shows that the core functionality is reporting issues with location and photos, and tracking status. The rewrite should focus on the functional scope of reporting and tracking, removing the abstract objectives.

3.diagnostic: No two valid documentary actions agree.

feedback.critique:
For 'Provide Real-Time Visibility and Trust Through Notifications': the original HLG incorrectly includes trust-building as a goal. Documentation confirms notifications alone serve updates; trust is not an explicit requirement. Preserve notifications while removing trust claims.

For 'Provide Real-Time Visibility and Trust Through Notifications': the HLG's description includes 'build trust in public administration', which is a high-level goal/objective rather than a functional requirement. The HLG'prime confirms that the functionality is specifically about notifying citizens of status updates via email and in-app notifications. The rewrite should focus on the functional scope of notifications.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the original HLG inaccurately groups private statistics with configuration. Documentation separates these into distinct functionalities. Preserve configuration while removing strategic decision-making claims.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': The original HLG is overly general. It should specify private access to detailed statistics and system configuration tools for municipal administrators to manage external company access and optimize resource allocation.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the HLG's description includes 'optimize resource allocation' and 'strategic decision-making', which are high-level objectives rather than functional requirements. The HLG'prime indicates the core functionality is managing urban reporting and external access configuration. The rewrite should focus on the functional scope of configuration and private statistics.

For 'Enable Citizen Participation in Urban Management': the original HLG overstates functionality by including tracking and transparency, which are not explicitly required. The documented scope is limited to reporting issues with location/photo and status updates. Preserve reporting while removing tracking and transparency claims.

For 'Provide Real-Time Visibility and Trust Through Notifications': the original HLG incorrectly includes trust-building as a goal. Documentation confirms notifications alone serve updates; trust is not an explicit requirement. Preserve notifications while removing trust claims.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the original HLG inaccurately groups private statistics with configuration. Documentation separates these into distinct functionalities. Preserve configuration while removing strategic decision-making claims.

For 'Enable Citizen Participation in Urban Management': The original HLG is too broad. It should explicitly mention reporting issues with location and photo, as well as tracking report status to foster transparency and civic engagement.

For 'Support External Companies in Managing Assigned Reports': The original HLG lacks clarity on secure communication channels for internal coordination between external maintenance personnel and municipal staff.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': The original HLG is overly general. It should specify private access to detailed statistics and system configuration tools for municipal administrators to manage external company access and optimize resource allocation.

For 'Enable Citizen Participation in Urban Management': the HLG's description includes 'foster transparency and civic engagement', which are high-level objectives rather than specific functionalities. The HLG'prime shows that the core functionality is reporting issues with location and photos, and tracking status. The rewrite should focus on the functional scope of reporting and tracking, removing the abstract objectives.

For 'Provide Real-Time Visibility and Trust Through Notifications': the HLG's description includes 'build trust in public administration', which is a high-level goal/objective rather than a functional requirement. The HLG'prime confirms that the functionality is specifically about notifying citizens of status updates via email and in-app notifications. The rewrite should focus on the functional scope of notifications.

For 'Support Administrative Oversight and Strategic Decision-Making': the HLG's description includes 'optimize resource allocation' and 'strategic decision-making', which are high-level objectives rather than functional requirements. The HLG'prime indicates the core functionality is managing urban reporting and external access configuration. The rewrite should focus on the functional scope of configuration and private statistics.

lowLevelGoals.critique: The low-level goals are mostly well-defined and align with the high-level goals, covering all key functionalities described in the software description. However, there is a minor omission regarding the anonymity option for reports, which is mentioned in the description but not explicitly covered as a low-level goal. Additionally, the low-level goal "Municipal Administrator views public statistics dashboard" is misaligned with its associated high-level goal, as it should be linked to the private statistics goal instead.

feedback.critique:
For 'Enable Citizen Reporting with Location and Photo': the original HLG does not mention the mandatory registration requirement, which is critical per documentation. Preserve all supported functionality (location selection, description, category, photos) while adding explicit support for mandatory user registration.

For 'Enable Citizen Reporting with Location and Photo': the reconstruction includes communication with municipal operators, which is not part of the reporting submission process. The original HLG focuses correctly on the submission of reports with location and media. The reconstruction should be narrowed to match the submission functionality described in the documentation.

For 'Track Report Status for Citizens': the original HLG excludes anonymous reports and external chatbot integration. Preserve notification and email updates while ensuring these apply to both named and anonymous reporters, and support external chatbots as documented.

For 'Track Report Status for Citizens': the reconstruction includes the ability to communicate with municipal operators and external chatbots, which are not part of the status tracking functionality. The original HLG correctly identifies the status tracking via notifications and emails. The reconstruction should be narrowed to match the status tracking functionality described in the documentation.

For 'Manage Report Lifecycle and State Transitions': the original HLG omits mandatory rejection justification for rejected reports. Preserve all state transitions while ensuring that rejected reports require a written explanation from the Organization Office.

For 'Manage Report Lifecycle and State Transitions': The HLG does not explicitly cover the 'Suspended' state. Include this in the description to fully represent the report's lifecycle.

For 'Manage Report Lifecycle and State Transitions': the reconstruction includes manual advancement of reports with optional rejection justification. The original HLG correctly identifies the review and approval/rejection process. The reconstruction should be narrowed to match the lifecycle management described in the documentation.

For 'Support External Companies in Managing Assigned Reports': the original HLG does not address the two cases for external company access (with/without system access). Preserve status updates and internal comments while ensuring both scenarios are supported, including manual resolution when companies lack system access.

For 'Support External Companies in Managing Assigned Reports': The HLG does not mention the restriction of internal comments to technical office staff. Add this detail to clarify communication boundaries.

For 'Support External Companies in Managing Assigned Reports': the reconstruction includes access to internal comments, which is not explicitly mentioned as a primary management function in the original HLG. The original HLG correctly identifies the management of assigned reports and status updates. The reconstruction should be narrowed to match the management functionality described in the documentation.

For 'Configure System Settings and External Access': the original HLG lacks explicit support for automatic assignment rules configuration. Preserve external access management while ensuring municipal administrators can define category-based automatic assignment rules.

For 'Configure System Settings and External Access': the reconstruction includes automated reporting workflows, which is not a primary configuration function in the original HLG. The original HLG correctly identifies the configuration of system settings and external access. The reconstruction should be narrowed to match the configuration functionality described in the documentation.

For 'Provide Private Access to Detailed Statistics': the original HLG does not distinguish between public and private statistics clearly. Preserve detailed statistical oversight while ensuring it is strictly for administrators, distinct from public statistics.

For 'Provide Private Access to Detailed Statistics': The HLG lacks specificity about the detailed statistics accessible by administrators. Specify these details in the description.

For 'Provide Private Access to Detailed Statistics': the reconstruction includes system performance oversight, which is not a primary statistical oversight function in the system. The original goal focuses on private statistics for administrative oversight. The reconstruction should be narrowed to match the statistical oversight functionality described in the documentation.

For 'Enable Citizen Reporting with Location and Photo': the original HLG does not mention the mandatory registration requirement, which is critical per documentation. Preserve all supported functionality (location selection, description, category, photos) while adding explicit support for mandatory user registration.

For 'Track Report Status for Citizens': the original HLG excludes anonymous reports and external chatbot integration. Preserve notification and email updates while ensuring these apply to both named and anonymous reporters, and support external chatbots as documented.

For 'Manage Report Lifecycle and State Transitions': the original HLG omits mandatory rejection justification for rejected reports. Preserve all state transitions while ensuring that rejected reports require a written explanation from the Organization Office.

For 'Support External Companies in Managing Assigned Reports': the original HLG does not address the two cases for external company access (with/without system access). For 'Configure System Settings and External Access': the original HLG lacks explicit support for automatic assignment rules configuration. Preserve external access management while ensuring municipal administrators can define category-based automatic assignment rules.

For 'Provide Private Access to Detailed Statistics': the original HLG does not distinguish between public and private statistics clearly. Preserve detailed statistical oversight while ensuring it is strictly for administrators, distinct from public statistics.
For 'Manage Report Lifecycle and State Transitions': The HLG does not explicitly cover the 'Suspended' state. Include this in the description to fully represent the report's lifecycle.

For 'Support External Companies in Managing Assigned Reports': The HLG does not mention the restriction of internal comments to technical office staff. Add this detail to clarify communication boundaries.
